Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on what we need to size pricing and an accurate POC: 

1) What we heard from you
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + guided responses for 10k monthly active agents, roughly 6–8M API calls/month.
- Target latency: sub-300ms p50 for short responses; longer async summaries acceptable.
- Budget guidance from procurement: target ~ $600–900 / 1M tokens (list price to procurement), with room for reserved capacity discounts.

2) Data we need to finalize a quote and PoC scope
- Realistic sample of input/output token stats (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, distribution). If you can’t share raw data, aggregated CSV works — sample CSV template attached.
- Peak concurrency and expected percent of requests requiring extended context (8k, 32k, 128k).
- Any special compliance requirements (we have Private/VPC options if data cannot leave your network).

3) Redwood action items (what I’ll send by EOD tomorrow)
- Ballpark pricing model and a worked example for your stated volume (6–8M calls / month) using three context profiles (predominantly 8k, occasional 32k, rare 128k).
- A sample token-profile CSV (attached) and a short plan for a 2-week PoC to capture real token usage.

4) Proposed next steps
- You: send aggregated token stats (or allow us to run a short telemetry pass during PoC).
- Us: deliver a tailored pricing worksheet + PoC plan.
- If everything looks good, procurement: draft SOW/PO and discuss reserved capacity options.

Sarah — really helpful, thanks. Based on the sample and your budget band, I ran a couple of worked examples to show unit economics and a proposal for a two-track PoC (measurement + performance). See the high-level calc below; I’ve attached a spreadsheet with line-by-line math (pricing_calc_1M_tokens.xlsx).

Assumptions (from your sample + our defaults)
- Monthly calls: 7,000,000 (midpoint of 6–8M)
- Avg prompt tokens: 1,150
- Avg completion tokens: 900
- Total avg tokens per call = 2,050 tokens
- Distribution by context window: 72% 8k, 24% 32k, 4% 128k (affects memory/instance sizing, not per-token pricing directly)

Worked examples (list price vs. reserved estimate)
- Total tokens / month = 7,000,000 * 2,050 = 14,350,000,000 tokens (~14.35B tokens)
- Per-1M-token target band (procurement): $600–750 list

Redwood illustrative landed pricing (we’ll formalize after PoC metrics):
- Hosted (on-demand): $1,000 / 1M tokens (fastest time-to-value, no commit)
- Dedicated reserved (12mo commit, partial discount): $600 / 1M tokens (list-band match)
- Private (VPC + enterprise support): $680 / 1M tokens (includes longer-term SLA + compliance add-ons)

Estimated monthly charge at $600 / 1M: 14,350M tokens / 1M * $600 = $8,610,000 (list estimate)
At $750 / 1M: $10,762,500

Notes on where costs come from and levers to reduce unit economics
- Context-length mix affects instance sizing and KV cache costs: high % of 32k/128k requests increases memory footprint and reduces batch efficiency.
- Batching and prefix/KV caching can reduce effective per-token compute by ~10–30% depending on hit rates. For your workload, we estimate ~18% reduction potential if we enable aggressive prefix caching for common prompts.
- Quantization / model selection: switching from fp16 to int8 equivalent stacks can reduce GPU hours per token by 20–40% (depends on model family).
- Autoscaling policy and reserved capacity: committing to a baseline GPU pool lets us offer the lower $/1M number — PoC should exercise production concurrency to justify commit levels.

Proposed PoC (2 weeks)
- Measurement week (Week 1): Instrument calls to capture token distributions, peak concurrency, and failure modes. We’ll run a telemetry agent or ask you to provide anonymized aggregates (we can accept CSVs).
- Performance week (Week 2): Run realistic traffic with our dedicated pool (small reserved slice) to measure latency, batching benefits, and savings from caching.
- Deliverables: finalized token-profile CSV, observed p50/p90 latency, projected monthly cost at different reserved tiers, recommendation for ideal context-window mix and model/quantization profile.

Next steps
- If you’re good with the PoC, we’ll issue a scoped SOW and a small trial credit to offset week 2 consumption.
- I’ll also schedule a 30-min tech sync with Monica (solutions engineer) to walk through telemetry and any redaction needs. Proposed times: Thu 3/5 10am PT or Fri 3/6 11am PT.

Attachment: pricing_calc_1M_tokens.xlsx
